  "text": "He looked at the key again. There was a strip of sticking plaster around its stem, yellow at the edges.

“What did he say?”

“That he was helping someone.”

She turned on the tap. Water struck the upper plate and spilled down her skirt. She moved back but left the plates where they were.

“Someone who lived there?”

“No one lived there.”

He picked up the photograph. Behind the gate, the downstairs windows reflected a sky much brighter than the one above the roof.

“When was this taken?”

“Look on the back.”

There was a date in pencil. Last Thursday. Beneath it, in smaller writing, a figure with a line drawn under it.

“That's more than his pension.”

“It's three years.”

“He's only been dead two.”

She shut off the water.

In the quiet he heard the neighbour's boy returning the bin, its lid knocking against the wall.

“He stopped paying before he died?”

“I suppose.”

“Then why send it to me?”

She dried her hands carefully, pulling the towel between each finger. He remembered her doing that at the hospital while his father slept with his mouth open.

“There's another photograph,” she said.

“In the envelope?”

“I put it away.”

“Where?”

She opened the drawer beneath the cutlery drawer. Among the tea towels lay a photograph facedown.

He reached for it, but she kept her hand on the corner.

“If we go,” she said, “we go in daylight.”

The photograph showed the same gate, newly painted. His father stood beside it holding a spade. Behind him, she sat in the car, watching an upstairs window."
